items.followUp: Define acceleration and state its SI unit.

rubric.why: Identifies force as a push or pull.
rubric.description: Force is described as a push or pull.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either term used as the definition of force.

rubric.why: States the effect of a force.
rubric.description: A force changes or tends to change an object's state of rest or motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that force changes or tends to change the state of rest or motion.

modelAnswer: A force is a push or pull that changes or tends to change the state of rest or motion of an object.
The SI unit of force is the newton (N).

items.followUp: State Newton’s first law of motion.

rubric.description: For every action, there is a reaction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an action has a corresponding reaction.

rubric.why: States the magnitudes and directions of the forces.
rubric.description: The reaction is equal in magnitude and opposite in direction to the action.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both equal magnitude and opposite direction.

modelAnswer: For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
The action and reaction act simultaneously on different bodies.

items.followUp: Write down two disadvantages of friction.

rubric.why: Recognises friction's role in enabling safe movement or holding.
rubric.description: Friction provides grip, allowing us to walk without slipping or hold objects.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid advantage related to walking, grip, or movement.

rubric.why: Gives another practical use of friction.
rubric.description: Friction makes writing possible, helps brakes stop vehicles, can light a match, or produces useful heat.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second valid advantage, such as writing, braking, lighting a match, or producing useful heat.

modelAnswer: Friction between our feet and the ground enables us to walk without slipping.
Friction between a pen or pencil and paper enables us to write.

rubric.why: Identifies the centre of mass as a point.
rubric.description: The centre of mass is a point in or associated with a body.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as a point.

rubric.description: The whole mass of the body may be considered concentrated at that point.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the body's mass is considered concentrated there.

modelAnswer: The centre of mass of a body is the point at which its whole mass may be considered to be concentrated.

items.followUp: Explain how a body behaves in neutral equilibrium when slightly displaced.

rubric.why: Describes the restoring behaviour of stable equilibrium.
rubric.description: A slightly displaced body in stable equilibrium returns to its original position.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the body returns to its original position after a small displacement.

rubric.why: Contrasts stable equilibrium with unstable equilibrium.
rubric.description: A slightly displaced body in unstable equilibrium moves farther from its original position or does not return.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the body moves farther away or does not return to its original position.

modelAnswer: In stable equilibrium, a body returns to its original position when slightly displaced.
In unstable equilibrium, a body moves farther from its original position when slightly displaced.

items.followUp: What is a contact force? Give one example.

rubric.why: Distinguishes field forces from contact forces.
rubric.description: A field force acts without physical contact between the interacting bodies.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the force acts without physical contact.

rubric.why: Identifies that the force acts through a field or gives a valid field-force type.
rubric.description: The force acts through a field; examples include gravitational, magnetic, and electric forces.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning a field or giving a valid example.

modelAnswer: A field force is a force exerted by one body on another without physical contact.
It acts through a field, such as a gravitational, magnetic, or electric field.

items.followUp: Name four devices that convert mechanical energy into electrical energy.

rubric.why: Rewards the first two valid device examples.
rubric.description: Names two devices that convert electrical energy into mechanical energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any two valid devices.

rubric.why: Rewards two further valid devices, giving four in total.
rubric.description: Names two additional devices that convert electrical energy into mechanical energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for two further valid devices; four valid devices are required for full marks.

items.followUp: Define one newton and one kilowatt-hour.

rubric.why: Defines the joule using work or energy.
rubric.description: One joule is the work done when a force of 1 N moves an object 1 m in the force's direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition of the joule, including the 1 N and 1 m conditions or an equivalent statement.

rubric.why: Defines the watt as a rate of energy transfer or work.
rubric.description: One watt is a rate of doing work of 1 J per second.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that 1 W = 1 J/s or giving an equivalent definition.

modelAnswer: One joule is the work done when a force of 1 N moves an object 1 m in the direction of the force.
One watt is the power when 1 J of work is done in 1 s; 1 W = 1 J/s.
